comparisons.peer_summary: The Corporation reports results through four business segments (Consumer Banking, Global Wealth & Investment Management, Global Banking, and Global Markets) and All Other, managed by the Management Team with the CEO as the Chief Operating Decision Maker for capital allocation.
comparisons.comparison: While both companies disclose their business segment structures, Bank of America reports four reportable segments plus 'All Other', whereas JPMorgan reports three reportable segments plus 'Corporate'. Bank of America's structure separates Global Banking and Global Markets, whereas JPMorgan has combined these functions into the Commercial & Investment Bank. Additionally, Bank of America explicitly identifies the CEO as the Chief Operating Decision Maker for capital allocation among segments, a governance detail not explicitly stated in JPMorgan's segment definition sentence.

sentences.text: As a result of the reorganization, the Firm has three reportable business segments - Consumer & Community Banking, Commercial & Investment Bank, and Asset & Wealth Management - with the remaining activities in Corporate.

The Corporation reports its results of operations through the following four business segments: Consumer Banking, Global Wealth & Investment Management, Global Banking and Global Markets, with the remaining operations recorded in All Other.
The Chief Operating Decision Maker of the segments, which is the Corporation's CEO, is the final approver on the amount of capital to allocate to each segment.

comparisons.comparison: Citigroup and JPMorgan differ in the number and composition of their reportable segments. Citigroup operates five reportable operating segments (Services, Markets, Banking, Wealth, and USPB), while JPMorgan operates three (Consumer & Community Banking, Commercial & Investment Bank, and Asset & Wealth Management). Both companies note that remaining activities are recorded in a catch-all category (Citi's 'All Other' vs. JPMorgan's 'Corporate'), and both structure their reporting around how the CEO manages the business.

comparisons.peer_summary: The firm manages and reports its activities in three business segments: Global Banking & Markets, Asset & Wealth Management, and Platform Solutions, which are organized based on products, services, customers, and counterparties.
comparisons.comparison: Both JPMorgan and Goldman Sachs report their business operations through exactly three reportable segments in 2024. However, the specific segment structures differ significantly due to JPMorgan's recent reorganization. JPMorgan consolidated its Corporate & Investment Bank and Commercial Banking into a single 'Commercial & Investment Bank' segment, alongside Consumer & Community Banking and Asset & Wealth Management. In contrast, Goldman Sachs has long maintained its 'Global Banking & Markets' segment (covering both investment and commercial banking activities) separate from 'Asset & Wealth Management' and 'Platform Solutions'.

sentences.text: Business segment reorganization: Effective in the second quarter of 2024, the Firm reorganized its reportable business segments by combining the former Corporate & Investment Bank and Commercial Banking business segments to form one reportable segment, the Commercial & Investment Bank.

As a result of the reorganization, the Firm has three reportable business segments - Consumer & Community Banking, Commercial & Investment Bank, and Asset & Wealth Management - with the remaining activities in Corporate.
The firm manages and reports its activities in three business segments: Global Banking & Markets, Asset & Wealth Management and Platform Solutions.
These business segments are determined and organized based on products and services provided, and the types of customers and counterparties served.

comparisons.peer_summary: The Firm operates in three distinct business segments: Institutional Securities, Wealth Management, and Investment Management, providing a wide range of financial products and services within each.
comparisons.comparison: Both JPMorgan and Morgan Stanley report three business segments. However, the specific segments differ. JPMorgan's segments are Consumer & Community Banking, Commercial & Investment Bank, and Asset & Wealth Management. Morgan Stanley's segments are Institutional Securities, Wealth Management, and Investment Management. Morgan Stanley's structure separates Wealth and Investment Management, whereas JPMorgan combines asset and wealth management activities into one segment.
